STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plate, typical range 20-30 cm. The plate looks medium-large relative to the table and the food, so I take about 25 cm side.
b) Reference: the chicken piece is roughly 10-11 cm across (about a drumstick-sized portion). The plate spans about 2.3 drumstick-lengths across, giving about 24-26 cm.
Final width: 25 cm, area = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Chicken (grilled/roasted, with crust): covers about 18% of the plate, about 112 cm². Thickness: a thick piece about 2.5 cm, averaging about 2 cm. Volume about 225 ml. Grams = 225 x 1.0 = 225 g. Hmm, the chicken looks fairly dense; I use 200 g.
- Roasted yellow squash/potato chunks: about 7% of the plate, about 44 cm². Chunky pieces, about 5 pieces stacked to 2 cm average thickness: about 90 ml x 0.6 = 55 g.
- Mixed greens (kale, spinach, arugula with tomato and nuts, cooked/dressed): about 25% of the plate, about 156 cm². Loose leaves, average thickness about 3 cm: 470 ml x 0.15 (raw leafy) gives about 70 g. Dressing and the nut/tomato garnish add a few grams, so I use 80 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer beyond the plate surface; the chicken is a single layer on the greens. No extra items.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Chicken with crust/oil: about 190 kcal/100 g.
- Roasted squash/potato: about 90 kcal/100 g.
- Mixed greens with dressing and nuts: about 60 kcal/100 g.

Total weight about 355 g. Energy: chicken 200 g = 380 kcal; squash 55 g = 50 kcal; greens 80 g = 48 kcal; total about 480 kcal.
